owned_invariants: read gives the graph a value denotes: a list of [u, v] pairs of text, which may be empty. Anything else gives nothing.
Vertices are numbered in the order the edges first name them, as in graph.rs, and names lists the vertex names in that order. A loop and a repeated edge are kept as written.
covers says whether a value is an object whose keys are exactly the vertex names.

by_name gives what a reader makes of the entry under each vertex name, in vertex order, and nothing when a vertex has no entry or the reader gives nothing for one. Entries under other keys are not looked at.
potential is by_name with the exact-rational reader, so a potential keyed by name comes back in the order the graph functions take.
boundaries: Vertex names are text. A task whose vertices are numbers is read by graph.rs, not here.
The numbering follows the edges, not the sorted names. A caller that wants names in another order asks names.
What a value on the vertices means for a verdict is each family's to say.

basis.G3: read, by_name and potential give nothing for what they cannot read, and covers is total. No panicking unwrap or expect, and no index. The one subtraction, in read, follows a push. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
